name: Lunar Lander
miniText: How does directing thrust trade off position correction against a safe descent? NetLogo Lunar Lander lets a player rotate a module and fire a thruster while gravity accelerates it toward generated terrain. A successful landing requires reaching the pad with sufficiently gentle motion. Acikmese and Ploen [1] develop constrained powered-descent guidance, Betts [2] surveys trajectory optimization methods, and Yang and Liu [3] examine fuel-optimal descent with path constraints. These are relevant scientific comparisons, not algorithms claimed to run inside the arcade baseline. The NetLogo model simplifies vehicle dynamics, terrain, and collision geometry; its Info explicitly notes omitted edge collisions. Thrust, attitude, and landing thresholds are discrete teaching rules without mission-calibrated parameters. The simulation illustrates feedback control and competing constraints, while success in the game does not validate a spacecraft guidance system.
